name: Sea-ice extent and area by hemisphere, 1991–2020 monthly climatology

source.dataset: NSIDC Sea Ice Index, Version 4 (G02135), monthly extent and area CSV files
references: Fetterer, F., K. Knowles, W. N. Meier, M. Savoie, A. K. Windnagel 2025, Sea Ice Index, Version 4, NSIDC
source.license: no restrictions; cite the data set (https://nsidc.org/data/g02135)

mask: sea ice of the ocean only, every sea cell including the polar cap: the passive-microwave product masks lakes and land, so the model's count takes its sea cells only, leaving its lake ice out, and takes the cells over the Arctic pole hole like any other
definition: Mkm², month m at index m − 1, each the mean over the month's days of a daily value cut at 15 %. Daily extent: the area of cells whose concentration that day is at least 15 %, the Arctic pole hole counted as ice. Daily area: the sum of concentration times cell area over the cells at least 15 % covered that day, with the Arctic pole hole added at full concentration (the files' area leaves the hole out; it is 1.19 Mkm² for SMMR through 20 August 1987, 0.31 for SSM/I from 21 August 1987 through December 2007 and 0.029 for SSMIS from January 2008, so in 1991–2020 the files' Arctic area is short by 0.188 on average); areaPublished is the files' area. The model's matching quantities are the same daily cuts of each day's mean concentration over its sea cells on these polar stereographic grids (neither land nor lake; the Caspian, the Black Sea and Azov lie off them; js/seaIceIndex.module.js), averaged over the window's days: spinup.mjs logs them at each day's end, to 0.01 Mkm² ("sea ice on day D's mean concentration, sea cells on the index's grids, 15 %"). A cut of a 30-day mean concentration is not the same quantity: it counts a cell iced for half the window as half covered. A hole at full concentration overstates the observed area by the open water inside the hole, a few hundredths of a Mkm² at most.

holes.source: Sea Ice Index Version 4 user guide (Fetterer et al.), the note on the monthly .csv files, p. 18: https://nsidc.org/sites/default/files/documents/user-guide/g02135-v004-userguide.pdf
